newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound wobbles on political uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound wobbles on political uncertainty.

text.p: The Lebanese pound initially continued its steady rise against the U.S. dollar for the first three days of the week but fell back slightly in interbank trade on Friday due to political uncertainties, dealers said.
The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band during the week to 1,540.5-1550 pounds per dollar from 1,541-1,550.5.
Dealers said commercial banks traded the pound from Tuesday to Thursday after the long Easter weekend at 1,541.5 per dollar -- one pound stronger than the previous week's interbank rate of 1,542.5.

However, Thursday's resignation of Constitutional Council chief Wajdi al-Mallat and the government's withdrawal of a bill to amend the municipal elections law sparked increased dollar demand on Friday and the pound fell back to 1,542.5 per dollar.
All demand for dollars was met by commercial banks without central bank intervention, dealers said.
The withdrawal of the elections bill caused concern among politicians and the media that the government might delay the first local elections since 1963 which are due in June.

"Trade among banks was quiet in the first three days of the week at one pound above the bid end of the intervention band," Talal Abou Zaki, Forex Manager for Bank Beirut and the Arab Countries said, "but due to political confusion on Thursday the dollar was traded two pounds above the bid end."
"The resignation of the head of Constitutional Council and indications of a postponement of municipal elections had some effect on the currency trade in the market," Abou Zaki said.
Mallat resigned amid reports that the Constitutional Council was facing heavy political pressures over appeals it is handling against the results of last year's parliamentary elections.

The withdrawal of the elections bill raised expectations of a possible dispute between Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and President Elias Hrawi who has made clear that he opposes any delay in holding the elections.
